newsitem.title: FRANCE: French broadcast body offering 300 radio licenses.
newsitem.headline: French broadcast body offering 300 radio licenses.

text.p: The Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel (CSA), the French broadcasting regulator, plans a tender for partial licenses to operate some 300 FM radio frequencies, its chairman said at the first meeting of a commission charged auditing FM frequencies in France.

Herve Bourges said on Tuesday about half the frequencies in the tender had been given back by operators who wanted to change category and half had become available because their operators had gone out of business or their authority to broadcast had been withdrawn, or by opening higher wavelengths.
A partial license will cover only part of the country.
Radio stations say there is an overall shortage of FM frequencies in France.

The prospect of a reshuffle of the waveband has prompted a row between leading general radio stations, which say they do not yet have national coverage on FM, and a leading music station, which says its audience and lack of FM frequencies justify it having priority over the general stations.

The CSA said the commission's job is to make the FM frequency's current use public knowledge, to plan for more profitable use of FM frequencies and to look at how to optimise the use of the FM band without favouring any particular category of radio station.
Its members include representatives of public and private radio stations, the culture ministry, legal and technical experts and representatives of two broadcasting companies.
The CSA is due to meet again on June 4.
